title: Debido a and a raíz de: giving the cause

sections.content: You know *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6. Both mean "because of" and are followed by a noun, not by a verb. They are the formal way to give the cause of a big change, which is what historians do when they explain why Latin American countries began to make things at home.

items.spanish: Debido a la crisis de 1929, los países pudieron comprar menos productos del extranjero.
items.english: Because of the crisis of 1929, the countries could buy fewer foreign products.

items.spanish: A raíz de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, llegaron menos máquinas a la región.
items.english: As a result of the Second World War, fewer machines reached the region.

items.spanish: Los productos importados eran más caros debido a los aranceles.
items.english: Imported products were more expensive because of the tariffs.

items.spanish: Debido a estas medidas, la industria creció en varios países.
items.english: Because of these measures, industry grew in several countries.

sections.content: After *debido a* and *a raíz de* put a noun (*la crisis*, *los aranceles*). Before a full clause use *porque* instead (*porque llegaban menos máquinas*). The phrase can open the sentence, followed by a comma, or come after the main clause.
